extracted.intended_audience: registered patent practitioners, attorneys subject to USPTO discipline, OED staff
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and standards for imposing reciprocal discipline on a practitioner before the USPTO when a state court has imposed discipline; includes procedural requirements, grounds of misconduct, and prescribed remedies. Focused on enforcement under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24 and related USPTO practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reciprocal discipline under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24
rubrics_metrics.description: Pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.24, the suspension imposed by a duly constituted authority of a State may be imposed reciprocally by the USPTO for violations of 37 C.F.R. §§ 10.23(a) and (b), via 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(c)(5).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office may impose reciprocal discipline identical to the discipline imposed by the State; new disciplinary rules effective May 3, 2013 do not preclude application of the prior USPTO Code to conduct occurring before that date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice and opportunity to respond (40 days) under § 11.24(d)(1)
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director must mail a 'Notice and Order Pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.24' to the respondent (here mailed by certified mail) and provide the respondent 40 days to file a response opposing imposition of reciprocal discipline based on the reasons in 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d)(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Notice and Order was delivered June 4, 2013; more than forty days passed with no response. Proper service and the 40-day period are procedural prerequisites to considering defenses under § 11.24(d)(1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure to respond → no genuine issue of material fact
rubrics_metrics.description: If the respondent fails to file a timely response to the Notice and Order, the Office may determine there is no genuine issue of material fact under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d) and proceed to impose reciprocal discipline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In this matter, Respondent did not file a response within the 40-day period, and the Acting Director determined suspension was appropriate based on that procedural default.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate reciprocal discipline equals state-imposed discipline
rubrics_metrics.description: When reciprocal discipline is imposed under § 11.24, the USPTO may order discipline that is identical to that imposed by the state authority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Here, the USPTO ordered a six-month suspension identical to that ordered by the Supreme Judicial Court of Massachusetts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Misconduct: holding oneself out as an attorney while administratively suspended
rubrics_metrics.description: Representing oneself orally, on letterhead, and in billings as an attorney with an office in the state without any limitation to patent law and without disclosure that one is not permitted to practice, after being administratively suspended.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This conduct was found to violate Massachusetts Rules of Professional Conduct 3.4(c), 7.1, 7.5(a) and 8.4(c), (d), and (h). Example manifestations: letterhead and billings implying active state licensure despite suspension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Misconduct: failing to respond to client and keep client informed
rubrics_metrics.description: Failing to adequately respond to a client's inquiries and to keep the client reasonably informed about the status of the case.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This conduct was found to violate Massachusetts Rules of Professional Conduct 1.1, 1.3, and 1.4. Expectation: reasonable communication and timely updates about matters under counsel's handling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Misconduct: misrepresenting licensure status to client
rubrics_metrics.description: Misrepresenting to a client that the practitioner was licensed to practice in the state and failing to inform the client of an administrative suspension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Found to violate Massachusetts Rules of Professional Conduct 1.4, 7.1, and 8.4(c) and (h). Key criterion: truthful disclosure of licensure and limitations on practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Misconduct: failing to diligently monitor a client's patent application
rubrics_metrics.description: Failing to diligently monitor the status of a client's patent application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Found to violate Massachusetts Rules of Professional Conduct 1.1 and 1.3. Practical expectation: counsel must track prosecution deadlines, fee payments, and USPTO notifications relevant to a client's application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Misconduct: misinforming client about abandonment and fee responsibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Informing a client that the USPTO made a mistake in deeming an application abandoned when in fact the practitioner failed to pay the appropriate fee, and failing to inform the client of the practitioner's error.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Found to violate Massachusetts Rules of Professional Conduct 1.4 and 8.4(c) and (h). Practitioners must accurately disclose causes of adverse events and their own errors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Misconduct: failing to turn over client file and protect client's interests upon discharge
rubrics_metrics.description: Failing to timely turn over the client's file and failing to take reasonable steps to protect the client's interests upon discharge, including failing to cooperate with requests to prepare an affidavit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Found to violate Massachusetts Rules of Professional Conduct 1.16(d) and (e) and 8.4(h). Expectation: upon discharge, counsel must cooperate to protect client's rights and transfer files promptly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sanction: suspension from practice before the USPTO
rubrics_metrics.description: Order that the respondent be suspended from the practice of patent, trademark, and other non-patent law before the USPTO for the period specified (six months starting on the effective date of the Final Order).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The suspension mirrors the state discipline and is the primary reciprocal remedy imposed under § 11.24.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remedy: publication in the Official Gazette
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall publish a Notice in the Official Gazette describing the suspension, the respondent's name and registration number, and the basis for discipline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Notice should summarize the state order and list the specific violations and rules implicated; disciplinary decisions are also posted in the OED Reading Room.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remedy: notice to state disciplinary agencies, courts, and the public under § 11.59
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director must give notice of the public discipline and the reasons for the discipline to disciplinary enforcement agencies in the states where the respondent is admitted, to courts where the respondent is known to be admitted, and to the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This ensures inter-jurisdictional awareness of reciprocal discipline and may affect reputational and licensing status in multiple jurisdictions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remedy: dissociation from USPTO Customer Numbers and PKI certificate
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO will dissociate the respondent's name from any Customer Numbers and the public key infrastructure (PKI) certificate associated with those Customer Numbers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical effect: the practitioner cannot act in electronic filing systems using those credentials while suspended.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restriction: prohibition on obtaining or being added to Customer Numbers until reinstatement
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall not apply for, obtain, nor have their name added to a USPTO Customer Number unless and until reinstated to practice before the USPTO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This prevents circumvention of the suspension by using existing or new electronic credentials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory authority for action
rubrics_metrics.description: The action is taken pursuant to 35 U.S.C. § 32 and 37 C.F.R. § 11.24.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Citations provide the legal basis for discipline and procedural authority for the USPTO to impose reciprocal sanctions.
